ADR-0180 (accepted 2026-08-10, GH #688): ui-conversation's declarative composition opt-in generalizes a reusable producer-side mechanism -- adopt-if-authored-else-create for a component supporting BOTH an imperative API and declarative light-DOM children, with identity ruled STRUCTURAL not path-dependent (clause 4, :78-89: addUserMessage/beginAgentTurn+AgentTurnHandle/reset/setContentRenderer/setEmptyState gain zero mode branches), and the rejected-alternative rationale against a parallel imperative surface on the adopted child (clause 2, :54-64: would duplicate the entire engine -- the exact two-implementations failure ADR-0129 clause 4 exists to prevent). Explicitly generalizes GH #666's setEmptyState/setContentRenderer path-independent seams and the TKT-0056/0058 composer-extraction precedent (Context, :29-31) -- the THIRD independent instance of 'let a consumer author a child instead of only driving an imperative API'. No row in agent-ui-component-patterns/SKILL.md's mechanism table or agent-ui-composition-patterns/SKILL.md's consumer table covers adopt-if-authored-else-create, structural (not path-branched) identity across an imperative/declarative dual contract, or the mint-no-second-API-on-the-adopted-child rule (checked 2026-08-12).

ADR-0181 (accepted 2026-08-11, GH #695) clause 4 (:81-88) mints field-location.ts, a store-key -> {pane, section, item} map explicitly DERIVED from the canonical constants ('never a hand-listed per-key table'), pinned total, fail-closed on an unmapped key -- citing its own precedent by name: 'the persona-patch.ts hoisting rationale applied again -- two hand-maintained enumerations of one truth is the GH #406 silent-divergence class.' This is the SECOND independently-cited instance of that exact failure class (persona-patch.ts, then field-location.ts) with a real named bug precedent (GH #406) behind it, and it is captured NOWHERE in the skill corpus: grep for hand-maintained/silent-divergence/PERSONA_STATE_KEYS/derived-from-the-canonical across .claude/skills/ hits only docs-author's unrelated derive-docs-never-hand-author law (a documentation-content rule, not this code-duplication rule) -- checked 2026-08-12. Candidate pattern for agent-ui-component-patterns: 'two enumerations of one truth' -- when a second lookup/map must exist over an already-canonical key set, derive it structurally (a pure function over the existing constants, parity-gated against real DOM/data) rather than hand-listing a parallel table.

ADR-0183 (accepted 2026-08-12, GH #740 + same-day ratified Amendment) mints the fleet's first shared, opt-in, progressive-enhancement browser-API seam: withViewTransition(mutate, enabled) + viewTransitionAvailable() living in components/dom specifically because it's 'the one home every same-document surface can import without a layering violation' (clause 1, :25-31), wrapped per-surface behind a default-false boolean prop on three independent hosts (router outlet, super-shell, and via the Amendment ui-surface-host), each byte-identical when unset. The Amendment (:65-102) additionally mints a reusable DETECTOR -- 'the host's OWN settled-once boundary' distinguishing first-paint streaming (never transition) from re-render (transition-eligible) on any incrementally-painted streaming host, resolving 'which grain is the transition boundary for a streamed surface' (cl.6's own framing, :54). ADR-0115 clause 7 explicitly flagged this as anticipated future work ('natural future candy') -- more opt-in-progressive-enhancement asks of this shape are expected. No row in agent-ui-component-patterns/SKILL.md covers a shared cross-surface opt-in-boolean seam for an optional browser API, nor the settled-once first-paint-vs-re-render detector for a streaming host (checked 2026-08-12).
